chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I said: Blood from a nosebleed or something else, or some semen, got onto my garment, and I marked its trace until I could get water for it. Then I got [the water], and the salat came, and I forgot that there was something on my garment, so I prayed. Then afterward I remembered. He said: “You repeat the salat and wash it.”

I said: What if I had not seen its place, but I knew that it had affected it, so I searched for it and could not find it, then when I had prayed I found it? He said: “You wash it and repeat [the salat].”

I said: If I thought that it had affected it, but I was not certain of that, so I looked and did not see anything, then I prayed and later saw it there? He said: “You wash it and do not repeat the salat.” I said: Why is that? He said: “Because you were upon certainty of your taharah, then you doubted, so it is not proper for you ever to overturn certainty with doubt.”

I said: If I know that it has affected it, but I do not know where it is so that I may wash it? He said: “You wash the area of your garment which you think it has affected, until you are certain of your taharah.”
I said: Is it upon me, if I doubt whether something has affected it, to inspect it? He said: “No, but you only want to remove the doubt that has occurred within yourself.”

I said: If I see it on my garment while I am in the salat? He said: “You invalidate the salat and repeat it if you had doubted about a place on it and then saw it. But if you had not doubted and then saw it wet, you cut short the salat, wash it, then continue on with the salat, because you do not know—perhaps it is something that fell upon you. So it is not proper to overturn certainty with doubt.”

key_terms.الشَّكِّ: doubt or uncertainty in contrast to established certainty
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْيَقِينَ: certainty, a legal state not removed by mere doubt
key_terms.ثَوْبِكَ: your garment, the object under discussion for impurity
key_terms.دَمُ رُعَافٍ: blood from a nosebleed that causes impurity on the garment
key_terms.رَطْبًا: wet, indicating possible recent occurrence of impurity
key_terms.طَهَارَتِكَ: your state of ritual purity or cleanliness
key_terms.مَنِيٍّ: semen, treated here as a source of ritual impurity on clothing

ai.seo_question: If I discover impurity on my clothes after salat, do I have to repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains rulings regarding najasah on clothing during salat and distinguishes between certainty, suspicion, and later discovery of impurity. It also states an important juridical principle: certainty is not overturned by doubt, a foundational rule in Shia fiqh concerning taharah and legal certainty.
